2609.12277.title: Reinforcement Learning over Patient Trajectories for Clinical Reasoning in EHR Foundation Models
2609.12277.paper_summary: Electronic health record (EHR) foundation models trained on longitudinal patient trajectories have demonstrated strong performance across diverse clinical prediction tasks. However, their clinical reasoning capabilities remain constrained by next-token prediction on limited and incomplete EHR data. To address this, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning framework that treats EHR foundation models as generative policies over patient trajectories. We formulate common clinical prediction problems (e.g., hospital readmission) as event-conditioned, time-windowed reasoning tasks. We then design time-aware, rollout-sensitive rewards to account for finite rollout lengths and temporally inconclusive outcomes. We find that RL fine-tuning consistently improves over pre-trained backbones and strong baselines. Notably, it enables smaller models to surpass larger pre-trained models in data-limited regimes and induces positive transfer across tasks. Further analysis shows that RL fine-tuned models generate trajectories with stronger structural and semantic alignment to ground truth and greater downstream utility.
2609.12277.paper_summary_zh: 電子健康紀錄（EHR）基礎模型在長期病患軌跡上訓練，已在各種臨床預測任務中顯示出強大的表現。<lb/>然而，它們的臨床推理能力仍然受到有限且不完整的EHR數據中下一個標記預測的限制。<lb/>為了解決這個問題，我們提出了一個強化學習（RL）微調框架，將EHR基礎模型視為病患軌跡上的生成策略。<lb/>我們將常見的臨床預測問題（例如，住院再入院）表述為事件條件、時間窗口的推理任務。<lb/>然後，我們設計了時間感知、滾動敏感的獎勵，以考慮有限的滾動長度和時間上不確定的結果。<lb/>我們發現，RL微調在預訓練的骨幹網絡和強基準上持續改善。<lb/>值得注意的是，它使得較小的模型在數據有限的情況下超越較大的預訓練模型，並在任務之間引發正向轉移。<lb/>進一步分析顯示，RL微調的模型生成的軌跡在結構和語義上與真實情況的對齊更強，並且具有更大的下游效用。
